chung.Learning-Teaching Method: - Offline.- Research-Based Learning (RBL) integration:Selected topics in this course are delivered using a lResearch-Based Learning (RBL) approach. Rather than converting the entire course into a full research-based subject, the course integrates one focused RBL mini-module in Unit 6 (E-Customs Procedures and Documentation), where students investigate declaration errors and documentary inconsistencies, analyze evidence, propose corrective actions, defend their decisions, and reflect on compliance implications. This design supports inquiry-driven learning, evidence-based reasoning, academic defence, and reflective practice while remaining feasible for a technical, application-oriented course in Semester 5.
chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description:
This course provides specialized and applied knowledge of electronic customs declaration and customs compliance in global logistics and supply chain operations. It equips students with the legal, technical, and procedural foundations required to understand customs administration; apply HS classification (Harmonized System Codes Classification), customs valuation, origin-related preferential treatment, and tariff/tax rules; and prepare and review e-customs declaration logic, supporting documents, and declaration flows for standard import/export and selected customs regimes. Through scenario-based learning, guided discussion, document review, and case analysis grounded in FIATA (International Federation of Freight Forwarders Associations) and VLI (Vietnam Logistics Research and Development Institute) resources, students develop compliance awareness, professional responsibility, and practical decision-making skills relevant to customs, freight forwarding, and international logistics environments.

- AI Tools will be used to support students in:

(1) generating ideas/structures for their speaking notes and slide structure of important topics of the course.

(2) editing the slide set after students have already finished it.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Students are responsible for preparing assigned materials before class, participating actively in in-class discussions and activities, and submitting all individual and group assignments on time.

- Laptops may be used in class only for academic purposes under lecturer guidance.

- Students should access the institutional LMS/portal regularly for announcements, materials, and assignment updates.

- Students are expected to work professionally in group activities and respect academic integrity in all assessed tasks.
chung.Tools: Internet; institutional FLM; presentation software; spreadsheet software for practice; AI-supported learning tools as directed by the lecturer
chung.Note: AI Policy: Students may use generative AI and other digital tools only as guided by the lecturer for idea generation, concept clarification, drafting support, document checking, and learning enhancement. Any AI use in assessed coursework must be disclosed clearly and students remain fully responsible for the accuracy, legality, and originality of their submissions. AI use is not permitted in quizzes and the final examination unless explicitly authorized. Students must verify AI-generated content against official customs/legal sources and comply with academic integrity standards.

clo: Explain the role of customs administration, trade compliance, and the legal-institutional framework governing e-customs operations in Vietnam within the context of global logistics and supply chain management.
Apply HS classification principles to determine appropriate tariff headings for typical traded goods and justify classification decisions using product information and legal notes.
Apply customs valuation, origin-related preferential treatment, tariff rules, and tax principles to determine customs value and payable import taxes in common customs scenarios.
Prepare and review the logic, data fields, supporting documents, and procedural steps of electronic customs declarations for standard import/export and selected special customs regimes.
Analyze customs compliance risks, liabilities, documentary errors, penalties, and professional responsibilities of customs declarants, brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics enterprises.
Use digital tools and AI responsibly to support customs learning, document preparation, and professional decision-making while maintaining academic integrity and ethical standards.

- Course introduction: course overview, assessment and learning expectations

UNIT 1. CUSTOMS ADMINISTRATION AND TRADE COMPLIANCE
1.1 Customs in global logistics, trade facilitation, and compliance mindset
- Customs as trade facilitator and control authority; compliance as an operational issue in logistics
Course outline; FIATA Manual Ch.1 overview; VLI introductory slides
Before class: preview the course outline and assigned pages. In class: guided discussion on why customs matters in logistics. After class: write a short reflection on customs and supply chains.

1.2 Vietnam Customs administration and key stakeholders
- Organizational structure, functions, and stakeholder roles
FIATA Manual Ch.1; VLI Ch.1 slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: stakeholder-mapping activity. After class: complete a stakeholder-role matrix.

1.3 Customs territory, operating locations, and customs-controlled areas
- Customs territory, operating locations, supervised areas, and logistics implications
FIATA Manual Ch.1; legal extracts on customs operating locations
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: concept check + short logistics-location case. After class: summarize how customs location affects procedures.

UNIT 2. CUSTOMS LEGAL FRAMEWORK AND CONTROL MECHANISMS
2.1 Legal framework for customs operations in Vietnam
- Law on Customs 2014; Law on Export and Import Duties 2016; Decree 08/2015; Decree 59/2018; Circular 38/2015; Circular 39/2018
Selected legal extracts; FIATA Manual Ch.2–3; VLI legal framework slides
Before class: skim the listed legal texts. In class: legal-framework mapping. After class: complete the legal-map worksheet.

2.2 Customs declarants: rights, obligations, and responsibilities
- Declarants, customs agents, brokers, and procedural accountability
FIATA Manual Ch.1–2; VLI customs formalities slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: short scenario analysis. After class: complete a declarant-responsibility note.

2.3 Import/export types and customs regimes
- Major import/export types and selected customs regimes relevant to declaration logic
FIATA Manual Ch.2 and Ch.5; VLI customs formalities slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: regime-comparison activity. After class: fill in the customs-regime matrix.

2.4 Customs inspection, supervision, and control mechanisms
- Inspection, supervision, control, and post-clearance overview
FIATA Manual Ch.2; VLI customs formalities slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: process tracing. After class: complete control-flow notes.
2.5 Risk management and customs channeling- Risk management principles, channeling, and compliance behavior
FIATA Manual Ch.2; VLI customs declaration and channeling slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: guided discussion + mini case. After class: note implications of green/yellow/red channels.

2.6 Administrative violations, penalties, and appeals
- Common customs violations, penalties, and appeals in practice
FIATA Manual Ch.1–2; Decree 128/2020 extracts; VLI penalty-related slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: penalty-mapping exercise. After class: complete the risk-and-penalty worksheet.

UNIT 3. HS CLASSIFICATION
3.1 HS system and nomenclature
- Purpose, structure, and logic of the Harmonized System
FIATA Manual Ch.4; VLI HS slides
Before class: read the HS overview. In class: concept explanation + structure exercise. After class: summarize the HS hierarchy.

3.2 GRI foundations and legal notes
- Section notes, chapter notes, heading text, and GRI 1
FIATA Manual Ch.4; WCO HS references
Before class: review assigned notes. In class: guided interpretation practice. After class: complete the GRI 1 note sheet.

3.3 GRI 2 and unfinished/unassembled goods
- Incomplete goods, unfinished goods, and goods presented unassembled
FIATA Manual Ch.4; VLI HS slides
Before class: read assigned examples. In class: example comparison. After class: write a short justification for two sample products.

3.4 GRI 3 for mixtures, composite goods, and sets
- Essential character and competing headings
FIATA Manual Ch.4; VLI HS slides
Before class: review examples. In class: classification discussion. After class: complete an essential-character worksheet.

3.5 GRI 4–6 and subheading logic
- Residual classification and subheading determination
FIATA Manual Ch.4; WCO HS references
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: guided practice. After class: summarize when each rule is used.

3.6 Classification by material, function, and end-use
- Product information required for sound classification
FIATA Manual Ch.4; VLI HS slides
Before class: prepare a product description. In class: attribute-based classification exercise. After class: improve your product description.

3.7 Composite products and multifunctional items
- Applied logic for difficult classification scenarios
Before class: read the case handout. In class: small-group analysis. After class: note the main classification challenge.

3.8 Common misclassification errors and consequences
- Revenue risk, compliance risk, and documentary consequences
FIATA Manual Ch.4; VLI risk examples
Before class: review error examples. In class: error-diagnosis activity. After class: list three prevention measures.
3.9 HS workshop A: consumer goods and retail products
Before class: review the worksheet. In class: classification workshop. After class: revise your answers.
3.10 HS workshop B: industrial, transport, and logistics-related goods
Before class: review the worksheet. In class: classification workshop. After class: revise your answers.

3.11 Advance rulings, disputes, and classification documentation
- Evidence, product specification, and customs communication
FIATA Manual Ch.4; legal extracts on advance rulings
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: documentation review. After class: prepare a classification justification note.

Quiz 1:
- Scenario-based MCQ quiz covering Units 1–3 (customs foundation, legal-control mechanisms, and HS classification)
Review notes and assigned readings for Units 1–3
Complete the in-class quiz individually and review feedback after class.

UNIT 4. CUSTOMS VALUATION
4.1 Customs valuation foundations and WTO framework
- Purpose, principles, and hierarchy of methods
FIATA Manual Ch.3–4; WTO customs valuation references
Before class: read the valuation overview. In class: concept explanation. After class: summarize the logic of valuation methods.

4.2 Transaction value method
- Primary method and conditions for acceptance
FIATA valuation section; WTO legal text
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: guided example. After class: identify the conditions for using transaction value.

4.3 Secondary methods I
- Identical goods and similar goods methods
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: method-comparison exercise. After class: note the differences between identical and similar goods methods.

4.4 Secondary methods II
- Deductive, computed, and fallback methods
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: method-sequence practice. After class: complete a method-selection worksheet.

4.5 Additions, deductions, and related parties
- Adjustments and valuation risk in related-party transactions
FIATA valuation section; VLI valuation slides
Before class: review the adjustment list. In class: adjustment-identification activity. After class: prepare a short related-party risk note.

4.6 Valuation workshop
- Applied valuation cases and method selection
Before class: review the worksheet. In class: applied workshop. After class: revise your answers.

UNIT 5. TARIFF AND IMPORT TAXATION
5.1 Customs tariff structure and duty types
- MFN, preferential, special preferential, and duty categories
FIATA Manual Ch.3; VLI tax slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: tariff-structure mapping. After class: summarize the major tariff categories.

5.2 Origin-related preferential treatment and C/O basics
- Origin in customs context and documentary relevance for tariffs
VLI origin section; relevant legal extracts
Before class: review assigned materials. In class: origin-preference discussion. After class: prepare a short note on the role of C/O.

5.3 Import duty calculation basics
- Tax base, taxable value, and basic import duty formula
FIATA Manual Ch.3; VLI tax slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: simple duty-calculation exercise. After class: complete practice questions.

5.4 VAT and other taxes in customs context
- VAT calculation and selected tax-related considerations
FIATA Manual Ch.8; VLI tax slides
Before class: review the VAT section. In class: guided calculation. After class: complete the worksheet.

5.5 Trade remedies and integrated tax application
- Anti-dumping, countervailing, safeguard duties, and integrated tax scenarios
FIATA Manual Ch.3; instructor scenario handout
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: scenario-based discussion. After class: complete the integrated tax scenario.

5.6 Tariff and tax workshop
- Integrated application practice for customs taxation
Before class: review the worksheet. In class: applied workshop. After class: revise your answers.

UNIT 6. E-CUSTOMS PROCEDURES AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 E-customs ecosystem and digital customs environment
- E-customs, National Single Window, ASEAN Single Window, and digital customs context
VLI declaration slides; Vietnam Customs NSW/ASW references
Before class: review the assigned materials. In class: ecosystem mapping. After class: summarize the role of NSW/ASW in customs digitalization.

6.2 VNACCS overview and electronic declaration logic
- Core system logic, data flow, and declaration structure
VLI declaration slides; FIATA Ch.2 and Ch.5
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: guided walkthrough. After class: complete a VNACCS logic note.

6.3 Customs dossiers and supporting documents
- Required documents, documentary logic, and document matching
FIATA Ch.2 and Ch.5; VLI dossier slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: dossier-identification activity. After class: prepare a document checklist.

6.4 E-customs flow for standard import shipments
- Sequence, control points, and documentary requirements
Before class: review the import flow. In class: process tracing. After class: summarize the import declaration flow.

6.5 E-customs flow for export shipments and selected customs regimes
- Export declaration logic and selected regimes
Before class: review the export flow. In class: comparison activity. After class: complete the flow-comparison note.

6.6 Declaration data fields and customs codes
- Key data fields, coding logic, and common data-quality issues
Before class: review assigned materials. In class: data-field exercise. After class: correct sample declaration data.

6.7 Channeling, inspection, and release decisions
- Green/yellow/red channels, inspection, and release logic within e-customs
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: channel-decision discussion. After class: note the implications for logistics operations.

6.8 Supplementary declaration, amendment, and cancellation
- Corrective procedures and documentary follow-up
Before class: review the corrective procedures. In class: error-correction walkthrough. After class: complete an amendment/cancellation scenario.

6.9 Special customs dossiers and selected special cases
Diagnosing declaration errors – problem framing

Printed or digital dossier pack

Error Identification Sheet

Initial RQ/Hypothesis Note template

Class slides / note-taking sheet

Before class: review the assigned dossier pack and identify potentially inconsistent fields or documents.
In class: work in pairs/groups to examine the dossier, identify errors or inconsistencies, formulate an initial research question, and propose a preliminary hypothesis.

After class: submit an Initial Error Identification Sheet and a short Preliminary RQ/Hypothesis Note.

6.10 E-customs document review workshop
Diagnosing declaration errors – evidence analysis

Dossier pack from Session 42

Completed Error Identification Sheet

Error Analysis Matrix

Corrective Action Decision Table

Before class: review the preliminary notes from Session 42.

In class: complete the Error Analysis Matrix,
identify the decisive evidence for each issue, and justify the most appropriate corrective route.

After class: submit the completed Error Analysis Matrix and Corrective Action Decision Table.

6.11 Common declaration errors, amendment logic, and corrective actions
Diagnosing declaration errors – defence and reflection

Finalized Error Analysis Matrix

Corrective Action Decision Table

Before class: prepare to defend your corrective-action recommendation.

In class: present and defend your case diagnosis, respond to peer/instructor questions, and refine your conclusion.

After class: submit a short Individual Corrective Action Memo and a Reflection Note on compliance risk and professional responsibility.

Quiz 2:
- Scenario-based MCQ quiz covering Units 4–6 (valuation, taxation, and e-customs procedures)
Review notes and assigned readings for Units 4–6
After class: submit the completed Error Analysis Matrix and Corrective Action Decision Table.

UNIT 7. COMPLIANCE RISK, LIABILITY AND DIGITALIZATION
7.1 Freight forwarder liability and customs brokerage
- Responsibilities, brokerage functions, and role boundaries
FIATA Ch.6; VLI customs responsibility slides
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: responsibility mapping. After class: prepare a short note on brokerage liability.

7.2 Compliance risk mapping for logistics firms
- Identifying procedural, documentary, tax, and declaration risks
FIATA Ch.6 and Ch.8; lecturer risk template
Before class: review the risk template. In class: risk-mapping activity. After class: complete the compliance-risk matrix.

7.3 Fraud, misdeclaration, and professional ethics
- Fraud patterns, ethics, and professional judgment in customs work
FIATA Ch.1, Ch.6, Ch.8; case handout
Before class: read the case handout. In class: ethics discussion. After class: write a short ethical reflection.

7.4 International conventions and frameworks I
- Kyoto Convention, HS Convention, GATT/WTO customs valuation framework
Before class: review assigned references. In class: framework overview. After class: summarize why international standards matter.

7.5 International conventions and frameworks II
- ATA, TIR, CITES, Bali TFA, RCEP, and ASEAN facilitation linkages
Before class: review assigned references. In class: small-group comparison. After class: identify one convention most relevant to logistics practice.

7.6 Other duties of customs administration
- Licences, veterinary/phytosanitary control, intellectual property, counterfeit, and related control roles
Before class: read assigned materials. In class: issue-mapping exercise. After class: summarize one non-tariff control area.

7.7 AI and digital tools in customs work
- Opportunities, limitations, and use cases for customs learning and practice
Before class: review the AI-use guide. In class: guided demonstration and discussion. After class: note one useful and one risky AI application.

7.8 Ethics, data integrity, and responsible AI use
- Verification, accountability, confidentiality, and academic/professional integrity
Lecturer AI-use guide; institutional integrity guidance
Before class: review assigned guidance. In class: data-integrity discussion. After class: prepare a short responsible-AI statement.

7.9 Final integrated review and exam preparation
- Course integration, review of difficult points, and examination guidance
Before class: review all units. In class: integrated review and Q&A. After class: prepare for the final examination.
